title: introduce-batch-cache-trimmer-and-tenant-quantizer-advisor
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: tenants with spiky traffic and long-lived prefixes were retaining large per-tenant prefix cache footprints, driving higher GPU memory pressure and per-token cost. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a safe, pluggable Batch Cache Trimmer that prunes low-value/idle prefix entries based on access-frequency + cost impact heuristics; and (2) a Tenant Quantizer Advisor CLI and light-weight service that recommends per-tenant quantization tiers (fp16/int8/4bit) with unit-econ estimates. The goal is to reduce unit cost while preserving tail latency and generation quality. High-level changes include a cache pruning pipeline (configurable windows and sampling), metrics/telemetry for cost delta estimation, a canary rollout strategy with automatic rollback on QoS regressions, and a new CLI endpoint to export suggested quant profiles per tenant with confidence bands. Checklist: [x] implement cache trimmer and integration hooks into serving runtime; [x] add tolerant fallback (no prune) under hot conditions; [x] quantizer advisor CLI + dry-run mode; [x] telemetry and new metrics (cache_pruned_bytes, prune_candidates, quant_recommendation_score); [x] e2e tests and canary manifest; [x] docs and release notes. Runtime changes are guarded behind feature flags and default to off for Dedicated/Private customers. Related: ENG-1428 (cache cost audit), ENG-1450 (quant policy MVP).
commits: feat(cache): add trimmer scheduler and pruning policy with pluggable heuristics
perf(cache): switch to approximate LFU sampler to reduce CPU during sampling
feat(cli): tenant-quant-advisor CLI and dry-run exporter
docs: add cache trimmer playbook and quant advisor user guide
test: add deterministic e2e for small-scale canary and unit tests for heuristics
ci: extend integration matrix to include tail-latency smoke test
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Can we bound the prune rate to avoid thundering herd on eviction? Suggest a token-bucket limiter - author reply: added rate limiter in trimmer scheduler and unit-tested behaviour.
Priya Kothari: Need a clearer rollback signal in case quality degrades - author reply: added QoS gate in canary manifest and a small evaluation harness to run prompt set A when rolling out.

Marta Ivanov: Is the quant advisor deterministic across runs? Concerned about oscillation - author reply: advisor now exposes a stability score and only recommends tier changes when stability>0.75 and expected unit-econ delta>5%.
SRE Team: observed one flaky tail-latency test on first CI run - author reply: reworked the test harness to use deterministic seed and re-ran pipeline.
release_notes: Introduce cache trimming pipeline to reclaim idle prefix cache and a tenant quantizer advisor CLI that recommends quantization tiers with unit-econ estimates. Feature gated and rolled out to canary first. Expected impact: 5-15% unit-cost reduction for tenants with stale prefix state; 2-3% platform-wide if enabled for medium traffic tenants.
testing_notes: Canary rollout 1) enable trimmer for internal-canary namespace at 2% traffic, 48h observation window, run prompt set A nightly to check quality; 2) enable advisor dry-run to collect model outputs and simulate quant impact; 3) if QoS gates fail, auto-rollback; logs and metrics emitted under redwood.cache.trimmer and redwood.econ.quant_advisor namespaces.
risk: Medium. The trimmer mutates in-memory prefix entries which can affect cache hit ratios and tail latency in worst-case synthetic patterns. Mitigations: conservative default windows, sampling-based selection, rate limiter on prune throughput, canary first rollout, and immediate fallback to no-prune when memory pressure is critical.
